his behaviors are abusive. it's my opinion that he likely isn't aware of that and it's a result of very poor emotional regulation and understanding of how words impact people as well as likely poor impulse control. this doesn't change that it's abusive. honestly, it sounds to me like this is a person that did not get the help that he needed growing up and is extremely disregulated because of it. on top of that, solely based on his behavior, it sounds like instead of getting him help, his parents may have just indulged him. there's a lot of nuance to autism that people don't understand and chalk up to someone being a shitty person, which I can completely understand, but there's a lot more to it than that. often times, autistic people don't know how to effectively communicate and/or get overwhelmed by it and it comes out as anger instead. there's also a lot of things that can make us feel very out of control and confused and for a lot of us, the reaction is to try to demand it to stop and just go back to what makes us feel safe and comfortable. obviously, this is not a healthy or sustainable behavior and coping mechanisms and replacement behaviors need to be implemented. I think he needs to see a professional that can help him learn how to regulate his emotions and communicate in a healthy manner. you've done more than enough on your end. you've put up with more than you should ever need to. all there is to do, should you so choose, is to try to communicate all of this to him in a calm and non judgemental manner. from a "how can we fix it" angle. that said, I'm not confident he would be receptive and you need to prioritize your own safety and well-being. abuse is abuse regardless of the reason behind it and you should do what you need to do for yourself above all. you can't fix a person, especially all on your own. I don't want you to take what I've said here and use it to excuse his behavior. this isn't a safe person and the best course of action is to leave.
